units.passage: For projects, GenAI would be used in S2 mode for the first individual projects and then students would transition to S3 mode for the large team project.
units.why: 'GenAI would be used in S2 mode for the first individual projects' is the committee's recommended plan for CS 321, addressed to the instructor designing the course, so instructor, before-course, should; it stages AI permission (S2 then S3) as skills develop, P08.

units.passage: Mynatt characterizes the approach as “crutch to coach to colleague” — a strong belief that while AI cannot replace a rigorous grounding in computer science fundamentals
units.why: "crutch to coach to colleague" describes staged AI use: reliance at the start is a crutch, later AI is a coach and then a colleague; P08.

units.passage: Only after students grasp these core concepts will they learn to use AI to accelerate coding tasks
units.why: "Only after students grasp these core concepts will they learn to use AI to accelerate coding tasks" states AI use comes after fundamentals, P08.

units.passage: Teach students how to do something without AI, and then once they’ve mastered that , allow them to cognitively offload that skill to AI ( Derek Bruff gives an example for Math and using Wolfram Alpha) so you can move them on to higher order knowledge and skills with the help of that cognitive offloading
units.why: "Teach students how to do something without AI, and then once they've mastered that, allow them to cognitively offload that skill to AI" describes staged permission after mastery, which is P08.

units.passage: Developing skills they will need before using AI responsibly in more advanced work
units.why: "Developing skills they will need before using AI responsibly in more advanced work" names a staged logic (skills first, AI later), so P08 and may.

units.passage: Education curricula in mathematics have adapted to the increasing availability of calculators to prioritize students’ learning basic skills without calculators at first, and later, allow and/or encourage their use to support higher level learning.
units.why: The calculator analogy says curricula prioritize 'learning basic skills without calculators at first, and later, allow and/or encourage their use'. That is permission staged as skill develops, so P08.
units.fit_note: Offered as an analogy for how AI permission could be staged. | Offered as an analogy for curriculum design, not as a rule.

units.passage: We recommend using GAI in advanced courses as a tutor or helper in programming, but not as the sole creator of code.
units.why: For programming it recommends GAI 'in advanced courses as a tutor or helper ... but not as the sole creator of code', which stages permission to advanced courses and bans sole AI authorship. P08 chosen; P12 (tutor) and P19 are secondary.

units.passage: After initially coding by hand in Leaflet.js to understand fundamental mechanics, students progressed to using GenAI for two purposes: solving specific, narrow coding problems and generating complete web map applications from scratch.
units.policy: Geovisualization students code by hand first to understand fundamentals, then progress to using GenAI for narrow coding problems and for generating complete web map applications.
units.why: Geovisualization students first code "by hand in Leaflet.js to understand fundamental mechanics" and only then "progressed to using GenAI", a staged permission (P08).

units.passage: Scaffolding can also help clarify at what stage(s) of the assessments AI is appropriate to use.
units.why: 'Scaffolding can also help clarify at what stage(s) of the assessments AI is appropriate to use' links stage to permission (P08 staged permission).
units.fit_note: Staging is by assessment stage within one assignment rather than across a course. | Staging is within one assessment, not across the course.

units.passage: takes into consideration the diverse teaching modalities in the unit (e.g., lecture vs. recitations vs. labs, off-campus and experiential settings, online courses, etc.), forms of assessment (e.g., tests, papers, projects, etc.), teaching loads, class sizes, and other considerations such as scaffolding a policy based on course level (i.e., more restrictions at the 100-level to more options at the 400-level)
units.policy: Unit policies take into consideration scaffolding a policy based on course level, with more restrictions at the 100-level and more options at the 400-level.
units.why: Units are asked to take "scaffolding a policy based on course level (i.e., more restrictions at the 100-level to more options at the 400-level)" into account; permission staged by course level matches P08.

units.passage: Courses designed for AI may incorporate AI for some activities and not others, and, depending on the course, AI may be explicitly excluded or included at different stages.
units.why: "AI may be explicitly excluded or included at different stages" in a course: permission varies by stage, P08.

units.passage: You will also see that GenAI is only permitted once you have practiced essential skills (such as analysis and critical thinking) yourself and can therefore better evaluate the quality of output from GenAI tools.
units.why: 'GenAI is only permitted once you have practiced essential skills (such as analysis and critical thinking) yourself' stages AI permission after skills are practiced; P08 fits.

units.passage: During the peer review stage, AI use is prohibited
units.why: Sample: 'During the peer review stage, AI use is prohibited': permission differs by stage of the assignment, P08.
units.fit_note: Stages within one assignment, not skills across a course. / Staging is within one assignment, not across a course.

units.passage: "When it comes to the final draft of your paper, AI use is also prohibited. At this stage, you will have everything you need to produce a polished draft, including feedback from me and two of your peers.
units.why: 'When it comes to the final draft of your paper, AI use is also prohibited' bans AI at the final stage after allowing it earlier, P08.
units.fit_note: Stages within one assignment, not skills across a course. / Staging within one assignment.

units.passage: For instance, could AI be helpful as a beginning-of-process tool (i.e., at the brainstorming or drafting stage of a project?) or would it be more suitable as an end- of-process tool (i.e., at the revision or final editing stage?
units.why: 'could AI be helpful as a beginning-of-process tool... or would it be more suitable as an end-of-process tool' asks instructors to decide AI's place by stage of work, P08 fits partly.
units.fit_note: Staging within a project, not across the course. / Stages AI by stage of the work (beginning or end of process), not by skill development.
